topic: Payment succeeded but the order was not created: why a slow payment webhook loses orders, and how saving the event first, placing the order from an Azure Service Bus queue and reconciling with the gateway every five minutes means every captured payment becomes an order.

title.sub: The payment worked. The webhook did not.

stages.title: The customer pays
stages.desc: Sunday lunch. ₹414 by UPI. The gateway captures the payment.
stages.narration: Sunday lunch. A customer pays four hundred rupees by UPI.

stages.title: The webhook does everything
stages.desc: The gateway calls your webhook. It updates the order, calls the restaurant, sends a push: 14 seconds.
stages.status: webhook · 14 s · gateway gives up at 5 s
stages.narration: The webhook does all the work. Fourteen seconds. The gateway quits at five.

stages.title: A restart kills it
stages.desc: An instance restarts mid-transaction. The order is never saved. The app was killed in the background.
stages.narration: A server restart kills it mid-save. The order stays pending.

stages.title: Ten minutes, then failed
stages.desc: An expiry job marks every order still pending after 10 minutes as PaymentFailed.
stages.narration: Ten minutes later, a cleanup job marks the order failed.

stages.title: The retry is ignored
stages.desc: At 30 minutes the gateway retries. The order is not pending, so the handler returns 200 and does nothing.
stages.narration: The gateway retries later. Ignored. A hundred thirty-one customers paid for nothing.

stages.title: Save first, answer fast
stages.desc: The webhook only verifies the signature, saves the event, queues it and returns 200.
stages.narration: The fix: the webhook only saves the event, queues it, and answers instantly.

stages.title: The queue places the order
stages.desc: A Service Bus queue hands the event to a processor. It places the order only if it is still pending.
stages.narration: A Service Bus queue places the order, and retries if anything fails.

stages.title: Twice? Nothing happens
stages.desc: A retried webhook hits the saved event and an order that is no longer pending. Zero rows change.
stages.narration: The same event twice? The order is already placed. Nothing changes.

stages.title: No webhook? Ask the gateway
stages.desc: Every 5 minutes a timer asks the gateway about every order still pending. Captured? Place it.
stages.status: timer · every 5 min · status by reference
stages.narration: And if no webhook arrives? Every five minutes, a timer asks the gateway.

stages.title: Save the event, ask the gateway
stages.desc: Save first, place from a queue, reconcile every five minutes. Only the gateway can say a payment failed.
stages.narration: Save the event. Ask the gateway.

end.title: Save the event. Ask the gateway.
end.sub: Webhook: verify, save, queue, 200. Queue: place the order once. Timer: reconcile every five minutes.

post.caption:
"₹414 gone from my account. Your app says payment failed." 💸

The payment worked. The order never got created.

WHY IT HAPPENS
The payment webhook did all the work in one request: update the order, call the restaurant, send a push. Under load it took 14 seconds. The gateway gave up at 5. A server restart killed the rest. Ten minutes later a cleanup job marked the order failed, and the gateway's retry was ignored.

THE FIX
1. Webhook: verify the signature, save the event, put it on a queue, answer 200. Nothing else.
2. Queue: place the order only if it is still pending. A duplicate changes nothing.
3. Timer: every 5 minutes, ask the gateway about every order still waiting.
4. Never mark a payment failed because a clock ran out. Only the gateway knows.

ON AZURE
Azure Functions for the webhook and the timer, Azure Service Bus for the queue, Azure SQL for the events and orders.

The gateway's event names in this short are illustrative, not any real gateway's contract.

Full write-up: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/payment-webhook-reconciliation-azure-functions

Follow for system design and cloud engineering tips.
